spec.name: strict-dispatch-returns
spec.intent:
Census measured 2026-10-03 against repository HEAD f9a73ae5e76c9848ea2e0f965c5cf9bb39f1ce66, with only the two handed design amendments uncommitted: records/design/01M4055P8KM691BD2WDBGF5QVK.json and records/design/01M4055WFZCMFSX97216YRCT18.json. This paragraph is the shared pinned census for this plan; architect-dispatch-contract cites it rather than repeating it. Repository source contains no outputSchema/schemaMode dispatch implementation or role output defaults. The dispatch occurrences are the delegation action, the architect role contract and role cell, and their four holders architect, nico, kino, mav (the complete observed declared-role dispatcher denominator). The planner additionally permits delegated census in its role contract; that optional…

Realize the dispatch-contract primitive as the canonical dispatch skill at packages/canon/src/skills/dispatch/skill.ts, using the existing Skill/formalBlock/composition pattern. This is the callable apparatus of the architect role, not a new architectural owner. State that each invocation declares its own strict return contract, delegates emit only conforming values, and invocation contracts supersede inherited/session or role defaults without requiring those defaults. A mismatch is a failed dispatch delivered to the dispatcher, not a design note, whole failure, semantic assay verdict or automatic redispatch. No schemas or transport fields belong to plans or units. Do not move the law into deliver, generic output formatting, forge or lifecycle state. Der…

For omp, document the native invocation-specific outputSchema and schemaMode strict path and consumption of parsed structuredOutput data, including addressed fields where available. Per the supported-harness law and the principal's 2026-10-03 ruling, Claude receives the same seam-owned intent at its highest available fidelity, but the projected skill must explicitly state that native Agent calls lack the machine-enforced per-call schema mechanism; print-mode --json-schema is not evidence of Agent-tool enforcement. Do not invent a delegation engine, use omp from Claude, imply parity, substitute role frontmatter, or silently degrade. Document the shortfall in the skill and the existing supported-harness user documentation.

Add focused canonical-skill and projection tests for the repository-owned skill, its invocation-contract guidance, and its emitted artifacts. The external omp enforcement mechanism is a precondition, not an output of this unit: the real strict-schema dispatch and parsed-object result reported in the handed cdd-dispatch-contract-handoff.md, sections What was tested and Confirmation from the task spec, are existing design evidence, not post-change acceptance. Do not require this implementer to produce a new live dispatch, exercise the external native validator, observe harness retry internals, or prove absence of external ledger mutation. Preserve the strict per-invocation contract and failed-dispatch law in the canonical and emitted skill; do not replace them with role-default schemas. Prove repository-owned contract construction with illustrative caller schemas and structured return fixtures, covering unit pinning, branch-required facts and closed object shapes. These are projection and contract-shape tests, not behavioral proof of harness enforcement; do not invent a validator or delegation engine, and do not label text assertions or mocked calls as native enforcement evidence. Update the existing delegation/return fixtures and their reach test to model a caller contract and structured value. This unit may project into temporary roots for its own proof, but does not update staged/deployed architect targets: that is the dependent adoption unit's sole ownership. Add a changeset and keep the single pinned census above as the shared planning evidence. Run only focused checks for these changes; full-project combination verification belongs to the integrator.

Resumption finding on 2026-10-03: the prior implementer reports that its only artifact edit is the uncommitted packages/canon/src/skills/dispatch/skill.ts in /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus; no commit or behavioral evidence was produced, and projection/tests/docs are unfinished. Preserve that partial file and reuse or correct it against this unchanged conceptual target; it is not accepted work. If work resumes in an isolated unit checkout, carry only that attributable file into the unit checkout without resetting, deleting or committing unrelated changes in the original checkout. The pinned census remains a historical measurement at its stated commit, not a claim that the newly added partial skill is absent. The unit remains active under legal in-place revision; neither a reset to pending nor a completion claim is warranted.
accept: The new dispatch skill is discovered by the existing plugin and projects through both supported adapters. Focused repository tests assert that the canonical and emitted skill require invocation-owned outputSchema with schemaMode strict on omp, consumption of parsed structuredOutput data, unit-name pinning for unit-scoped calls, mismatch-as-failed-dispatch, and no automatic redispatch. These tests fail if those requirements are removed or replaced by role-default-as-contract guidance; they test the changed corpus/projection, not the pre-existing harness enforcement implementation.

Loop guidance and illustrative caller-contract fixtures cover the actual receiving-role result branches: planner ready/waiting/closed, implementer landed/blocked, assayer achieved/not-achieved with missing-part addresses, and integrator whole/red and plan-close, without forcing an ad-hoc request into those shapes. Contract-shape tests assert the contextual names, conditional required facts, unit const for each unit-scoped example, and closed object properties; wrong-unit, missing-required-data and extra-property/prose controls identify the schema constraints they violate without claiming to exercise the native validator. No schema or transport field is added to any plan/unit model, capability or record, and no return-format law is installed in deliver or a generic output-format cell.

The changed user documentation explicitly separates repository-owned projection/contract proof from external omp enforcement, identifying the existing live strict-schema POC in the handed cdd-dispatch-contract-handoff.md as design evidence for the harness precondition. No pre-change POC, mock, text assertion or environment failure is reported as post-change native dispatch refusal evidence. A new live harness run and retained native-validator results are not unit acceptance requirements.

Repository tests assert that the canonical and emitted mismatch guidance returns a failed dispatch to its dispatcher and expressly excludes automatic redispatch, design-note creation, whole failure, semantic assay verdict and lifecycle-state mutation as mismatch handling. The unit adds no runtime retry, note, whole or plan/unit state-write path. This criterion concerns the changed instructions and artifact footprint; it requires no observation of external harness internals or execution against a live plan.

Projection tests read the emitted Claude dispatch skill and assert an explicit machine-enforcement shortfall, while preserving caller-owned seam intent. They reject a claim that native Claude Agent calls enforce the omp transport or that role output defaults compensate. The supported-harness documentation states the real difference and cites https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.

Updated delegation/return fixtures exercise the structured seam, and reader-reach plus dispatch-contract focused tests pass. Reach proof prints the complete inspected fixture/harness denominator. A changeset records the user-visible contract; no generated/staged/host artifacts owned by architect-dispatch-contract are modified.
